channel.title: Weekly Worker — Capitalism & Crisis (unofficial)
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of articles published by Weekly Worker — Capitalism & Crisis.

item.title: Funny, if only
item.description: Anthropic’s initial public offering was the biggest in history. But the bumpy ride for tech stocks continues, as does political controversy over the AI industry. Paul Demarty investigates the bubble
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: If loving you is Huang …
item.description: The underlying dynamic, of dividing the world into great-power blocs pending great-power war, has been drastically reinforced by - of all things - the sexual exploits of a middle-aged, leather-jacketed nerd. Harley Filben looks at Nvidia and its strategic importance
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: The great AI swindle
item.description: Caught between faltering returns and lower-priced competition from China’s state-directed tech industry, the east Asian AI bubble is bursting. How will this affect the US? The big test will be the public launch of Anthropic, writes Michael Roberts
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Monumental crash beckons
item.description: Capitalist states face huge problems with high interest rates, low economic growth and ballooning government and corporate debt. Ted Reese says the system is in deep trouble and seems to be running out of options
item.dc:creator: Ted Reese

item.title: Pouvoir d’achat crisis
item.description: State education is in an advanced stage of decay. Over the last decade real spending per student has plummeted. Meanwhile the cost of living has soared, along with government borrowing costs. Michael Roberts investigates
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts
